result:
The proposed answer c = 1 can't be right, because it doesn't give a refinement of the earlier bound n ≤ 2m−3.

For k = 3, the formula with c = 1 gives n ≤ 2m − ⌊4/2⌋ = 2m−2. That is weaker than n ≤ 2m−3, so it is not a refinement. A refinement must give at least 2m−3 at k = 3, which needs ⌊(3+c)/2⌋ ≥ 3, so c ≥ 3. The true constant is therefore at least 3. I believe it is 3 or 4, but I can't pin it down from memory. Either way it is not 1.

The proposed solution never derives c. It only says that 1 is "the most likely intended value."

VERDICT: REJECT
